subject: pm fees are bigger than you think
preheader: 8 percent is just the headline. then come the extras.
headline: The 8% PM fee everyone quotes is the marketing number. The real load is closer to 12%.
body: Property management quotes 8-10% of gross rent. That's the monthly fee. It is not the total cost.

Add a leasing fee — typically one full month's rent every time you turn a tenant. If your tenant stays one year, that's another 8% annualized. If they stay two years, 4%. Renewal fees on top — usually $150-400 when the same tenant re-signs.

Then the misc stuff. Maintenance markups (10-15% on top of contractor invoices). Inspection fees. Lease-up advertising costs. Eviction handling. The 'full-load' PM cost in most markets is 11-14% of gross rent, not 8%.
On a $2,000/mo rental, the difference between modeling 8% and 12% is $80/mo or $960/yr. That can be the entire margin between an 8% cash-on-cash and a 6% one.
When you underwrite, use 10% as the floor, 12% as the realistic figure unless you have a specific PM contract in hand. TrueCap defaults to 10% and lets you bump it. Most pros bump it.
